subject: Business Models
title: Circular Economy Models
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Circular Economy Models.

hook.text: Patagonia tells customers: 'Don't buy this jacket.' Its business model profits from less consumption, not more.

buildup.text: Circular economy models design products for reuse, repair, and recycling instead of disposal.

discovery.text: Patagonia's Worn Wear program resells used jackets. Customers stay loyal and the brand strengthens with each cycle.

twist.text: Patagonia's founder gave away the company to fight climate change. The model proves purpose and profit can coexist.

climax.text: Circular models attract premium-paying customers who value sustainability. Ethics becomes a competitive advantage.

punchline.text: 'Don't buy this jacket' increased sales. Sustainability can be a business model.

quiz.question: How does Patagonia's circular model strengthen its business?
options: Customer loyalty and premium pricing through sustainability values

details.summary: Circular economy models replace the traditional make-use-dispose pattern with systems designed for reuse, repair, refurbishment, and recycling. Revenue comes from product life extension, material recovery, or access-based services rather than single-use product sales.
details.whyItMatters: Linear business models waste resources and create pollution. Circular models capture value from products multiple times, reduce raw material costs, meet growing sustainability regulations, and appeal to environmentally conscious consumers.
takeaways: Products are designed for durability, repairability, and recyclability
Revenue models shift from ownership sales to access and service fees
Material recovery and refurbishment create additional revenue streams

faq.question: What are common circular economy business model types?
faq.answer: Product-as-a-service retains ownership and charges for use. Resale and refurbishment extend product life through secondary markets. Take-back programs recover materials for recycling. Sharing platforms maximize utilization of existing products across multiple users.

faq.question: Are circular business models actually profitable?
faq.answer: Yes, when designed well. Patagonia's repair program increases customer loyalty. Apple's refurbished devices capture additional margin. Interface carpets save on raw materials through recycling. The key is designing circularity in from the start rather than adding it later.
